$comment: Read from the SIA chart set AD 2 LFKP (AIP France, chart dated 2025-03-20): the reporting points come from the coordinates table of the chart,
the notes from the English column of its text pages, both read by a script and checked (each point lies within 80 NM of the aerodrome).
Only what the chart prints is recorded; nothing is deduced. Services, frequencies, elevation, position, magnetic variation and runways
were first extracted automatically from the chart text. Drawings (circuit, routes, radials) are not read.
The charts themselves are (c) SIA and are not redistributed. Flight simulation only: never use for real navigation.

A "fr" object holds the French column of the same chart, copied as printed and never translated: a French note sits at the index of its English twin and is left empty when the twin could not be paired with certainty; the French of the procedures and of the points' purposes is not recorded.
name: Tour-du-Pin - Cessieu

source.extraction: chart text, table and English column read by script, checked
source.frenchExtraction: French column of the chart text, read by script and paired with the English sentences

notes: AD reserved to ACFT and gliders whom pilots had been recognized able to use AD, by an instructor (or holding an instructor qualification).
Usable by HEL and ULM.
Usable declared distances: TODA RWY 11 and RWY 29 reduced to take into account obstacles in TKOF funnels.
Convex RWY: aligned ACFT are not visible from the opposite THR.
Hill East of the airfield with a large angle of 2.7° / 4.7% (from the East end of RWY 11).
Hill before THR 29: can create the illusion of being too low on the plan.
Possible air turbulence and descending air currents on final.
Presence of birds due to the waste reception centre in the East of the AD.
In case of gliding activity, possible absence of the dihedrals of RWY North-East or North-West angles.
Preferential QFU 292° due to hill East of the airfield.
TKOF RWY 29: after take-off, follow MAG 280°.
South AD traffic pattern for helicopters and class 3 ULM.
Limitation of noise emissions: Non home-based ACFT: avoid exceeding 3 consecutive AD circuits; HEL: limit prolonged hovering flights.
Aérodrome réservé aux avions et planeurs dont les pilotes ont été reconnus aptes à utiliser l'aérodrome par un instructeur (ou détiennent une qualification d'instructeur).
Utilisable par les HEL et ULM.
Distances déclarées utilisables : TODA RWY 11 et RWY 29 réduites afin de tenir compte des obstacles dans les trouées de TKOF.
Piste convexe : les ACFT alignés ne sont pas visibles du seuil opposé.
Colline à l'Est du terrain avec un angle important de 2,7° / 4,7% (à partir de l'extrémité Est de la piste 11).
Colline avant le seuil 29 : peut créer l'illusion d'être trop bas sur le plan.
Turbulences et rabattants possibles en finale.
Présence d'oiseaux générée par la déchetterie à l'Est du terrain.
En cas d'activité VAV, absence possible des dièdres des angles Nord-Est ou Nord-Ouest de la piste.
QFU 292° préférentiel cause colline à l'Est de l'AD.
TKOF RWY 29 : après le décollage, prendre la RM 280°.
Tour de piste au Sud pour les hélicoptères et les ULM de classe 3.
Limitations des nuisances sonores : Aéronefs non basés : éviter de dépasser 3 tours de piste consécutifs ; HEL : limiter les vols stationnaires prolongés.
